rows.title: Economists concerned after labour market sheds jobs for third month in a row
rows.summary: Statistics Canada's October Labour Force Survey showed the economy lost 4,700 jobs, while economists polled by Reuters had expected a gain of about 13,600. The unemployment rate rose 0.2 percentage points to 6.7%, a six-month high, as more people looked for work, following roughly 110,000 job losses across August and September. Private-sector employment fell by 53,000, the first drop since February, while public-sector hiring rose by 50,000, and youth unemployment climbed to 13.7%. Average hourly wage growth slowed to 2.2% year over year. The report came about a week after the Bank of Canada raised its policy rate a quarter point to 2.5%, its first hike in more than three years, to get ahead of inflation from a global energy shock.
rows.fact: Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October and the unemployment rate rose to 6.7%. Private-sector employment dropped by 53,000 while public-sector jobs rose by 50,000, and wage growth eased to 2.2%.
rows.outlook: CIBC's Andrew Grantham expects the Bank of Canada to hold in December if labour data stays soft and oil prices keep falling, while Capital Economics sees at most two more precautionary hikes.
rows.why: 중앙은행이 물가를 잡으려고 금리를 올리는 동안 일자리가 줄어드는 상황을 보여 주어, 인플레이션 억제와 고용 사이의 상충 관계를 이해하게 해 준다.
rows.why_en: It shows jobs being lost even as the central bank raises rates to fight inflation, which teaches the trade-off between controlling inflation and protecting employment.
rows.term_def: Unused capacity in the job market: more people want work, or more hours, than employers are hiring for. When slack is high, wages tend to rise slowly.
rows.note: Key figures match Reuters' version (via BNN Bloomberg) and TD Economics' note on the Statistics Canada release.

opinion.title: Canadian Employment (October 2026)
opinion.author: Andrew Hencic (Director & Senior Economist)
opinion.summary: Hencic calls October the third straight disappointing labour report, pointing to large job losses, a job-finding rate of 18.9% that is well below its 2017-19 average, and a still-growing labour force as signs of more slack. He argues that soft wage growth means labour demand is not outpacing supply, which limits inflation pressure from wages even after the Bank of Canada's recent 'risk management' rate hike. Because weak earnings leave consumers little room to absorb higher prices, he doubts businesses can fully pass on energy-driven costs, and he expects soft momentum through year-end.
opinion.why: 임금 상승률과 구직 성공률 같은 지표로 노동시장의 여유를 판단해 금리 정책을 예측하는 방법을 배울 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how economists use wage growth and job-finding rates to judge labour market slack and predict interest-rate policy.

rows.title: US trade deficit narrows slightly in September as imports hit record high
rows.summary: Commerce Department data showed the U.S. goods and services trade deficit narrowed 0.7% in September to $105.0 billion, smaller than the roughly $108 billion economists expected. Imports still rose 1.2% to a record $426.6 billion, led by an $11.6 billion jump in capital goods such as computers bought for the AI data-center buildout, while exports grew 1.9% to $321.5 billion. Economists estimated that computers, peripherals and semiconductors made up roughly 61% of the deficit. Despite tariffs, goods deficits with Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan and South Korea reached records. Imports subtracted 2.64 percentage points from third-quarter GDP growth, the biggest drag since early 2025.
rows.fact: The September trade gap shrank slightly to $105.0 billion, but imports hit an all-time high as companies imported large amounts of AI computer hardware. Adjusted for inflation, the goods deficit actually widened 3.0% to $119.5 billion, with record bilateral deficits with Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan and South Korea.
rows.outlook: Capital Economics questioned whether AI-related imports can keep growing this fast, and inflation is expected to stay above the Fed's 2% target into 2027.
rows.why: 관세를 올려도 AI 투자 붐으로 수입이 사상 최대를 기록한 사례를 통해, 무역수지가 관세보다 국내 투자와 수요에 더 크게 좌우되며 수입이 GDP 계산에서 차감된다는 원리를 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: This record-import month during a tariff era shows that the trade balance depends more on domestic investment and demand than on tariffs, and how imports are subtracted when GDP is calculated.
rows.term_def: The amount by which what a country buys from abroad (imports) exceeds what it sells abroad (exports) over a period.
rows.note: Official Commerce Department data released Nov. 4 (U.S. time); figures cross-checked against Bloomberg's report via Transport Topics.

opinion.title: Breitbart Business Digest: Trump's Tariffs Are Bringing Down the Trade Deficit
opinion.author: John Carney
opinion.summary: Carney, writing from a pro-tariff perspective, argues that the September data understate how much tariffs are shrinking the trade deficit because surging AI data-center imports hide the improvement. Citing Harvard economist Jason Furman's figures, he says the deficit excluding data-center goods fell to about 0.7% of GDP from roughly 2.2-2.3% in the same period of 2024 and 2025. He calls tariff exemptions for AI hardware sensible, and says the import dependence shows America needs to rebuild domestic manufacturing.
opinion.why: 같은 무역 통계라도 어떤 품목을 빼고 보느냐에 따라 관세 정책의 성과가 다르게 보인다는 점을 보여 주어, 경제 데이터를 비판적으로 해석하는 연습을 할 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: The same trade numbers can make tariffs look effective or ineffective depending on which goods you exclude, so this one-sided column is good practice in reading economic data critically.

rows.title: South Korea posts record $61.46 billion current account surplus on chip exports
rows.summary: The Bank of Korea said South Korea's current account surplus hit a record $61.46 billion in September, the first monthly surplus above $60 billion and far above June's previous record of $49.73 billion. Surging semiconductor shipments drove the result: goods exports jumped 92.4% from a year earlier to $130.72 billion while imports rose 29.4%, leaving a record goods surplus of $62.75 billion. The services deficit widened to $3.35 billion as Koreans spent more on overseas travel and foreign intellectual property. The current account has stayed in surplus every month since May 2023, and the January-September total of $340.66 billion is about four times the same period of 2025.
rows.fact: September's current account surplus was $61.46 billion, up from $46.11 billion in August and $14.22 billion a year earlier. The goods surplus hit a record $62.75 billion, primary income showed a $2.65 billion surplus on higher dividend income, and services ran a $3.35 billion deficit.
rows.why: 반도체 수출 호황이 경상수지라는 국가 '가계부'에 어떻게 나타나는지, 그리고 상품·서비스·소득수지가 서로 다른 방향으로 움직일 수 있다는 국제수지의 구조를 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a chip export boom appears in a country's 'household ledger', the current account, and that the goods, services and income balances can move in different directions.
rows.term_def: A country's record of money flowing in and out from trade in goods and services plus income such as dividends and wages; a surplus means more came in than went out.
rows.note: Bank of Korea data released Nov. 5. The nine-month comparison is computed from the article's figures (about four times).

opinion.title: Record Current-Account Surplus Masks Capital Flight From Korea
opinion.author: Editorial Board
opinion.summary: The editorial board welcomes the record surplus but worries that the money is not staying in Korea, noting net financial outflows of about $303.6 billion in the first nine months, nearly equal to the surplus. Koreans have piled into foreign securities and direct investment abroad, while foreign investors cut net holdings of Korean securities and inbound direct investment was only about a third of outbound. It warns that heavy reliance on semiconductors could leave the economy facing a growth cliff when the chip cycle turns, and calls for deregulation and structural reform to draw investment home.
opinion.why: 경상수지 흑자로 벌어들인 돈이 해외 투자로 빠져나가는 '금융계정'의 의미를 통해, 수출 실적만으로는 경제의 체력을 판단할 수 없다는 점을 생각해 볼 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: By explaining the financial account, where money earned through a current account surplus flows out as overseas investment, it shows why strong exports alone do not prove an economy is healthy.

rows.title: Eurozone inflation climbs to 4% in October on spike in energy costs
rows.summary: Eurostat's flash estimate showed consumer prices in the 21-country euro area rose 4.0% year on year in October, up from 3.8% in September and twice the European Central Bank's 2% target. It is the highest rate since September 2023. Energy prices drove most of the rise, climbing 20.8% from a year earlier, a jump AFP links to the war in the Middle East. Core inflation, which excludes energy and food, held at 2.5%, and food and drink inflation edged up to 1.6%. The ECB held rates the previous week but left the door open to raising them in December.
rows.fact: Eurostat put October euro-area inflation at 4.0%, up from 3.8%, with energy prices up 20.8% and core inflation unchanged at 2.5%. The figure matched economists' forecasts and is the highest since September 2023.
rows.outlook: Analysts expect one more ECB rate hike this year, with Capital Economics seeing a December hike as probably the last of the cycle.
rows.why: 에너지 가격 같은 공급 충격이 물가를 끌어올릴 때 중앙은행이 왜 경기가 약한데도 금리 인상을 고민하는지, 헤드라인 물가와 근원 물가를 구분해 보는 법을 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: It shows why a central bank may consider raising rates even in a weak economy when an energy supply shock lifts prices, and how to tell headline from core inflation.
rows.term_def: Headline inflation counts all prices; core inflation leaves out volatile energy and food to show the underlying trend.

opinion.title: Eurozone October inflation brings ECB closer to December hike
opinion.author: Carsten Brzeski (ING Global Head of Macro)
opinion.summary: Brzeski notes that stable core inflation of 2.5% suggests higher energy prices have so far spread little into the rest of the economy. He argues this wave differs from 2022 because consumers are less willing and able to accept higher prices, so firms will struggle to pass on costs and will see margins squeezed instead. He expects headline inflation to worsen before improving, with oil, the Middle East war and winter gas prices as key risks, and thinks a December ECB hike has become more likely but could be the last one.
opinion.why: 같은 물가 상승이라도 기업이 비용을 소비자 가격에 전가할 수 있는지(2차 효과)에 따라 중앙은행의 대응이 달라진다는 점을 보여 준다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that a central bank's response to rising prices depends on whether firms can pass higher costs on to consumers (second-round effects).

rows.title: China's producer prices top forecasts in October
rows.summary: China's factory-gate prices rose 5.7% year on year in October, according to the National Bureau of Statistics, beating the 5.3% economists expected and marking the fastest rise since June 2022. Consumer inflation moved the other way, slowing to 0.7% from 0.9% in September, well below Beijing's target of about 2%. Producer prices have climbed since the Iran war began in late February, ending more than three years of falling factory prices, with higher global energy costs and AI-related electronics as the main drivers. Weak household spending and a lingering property debt crisis mean rising business costs are not turning into broad price increases for shoppers.
rows.fact: October PPI rose 5.7% year on year against a 5.3% forecast, while CPI rose 0.7% against a 0.8% forecast. China's GDP grew 4.5% in the third quarter, against a 2026 growth target of 4.5-5%.
rows.outlook: Capital Economics expects the external price shock to persist for a few months, then fade next year, with producer prices falling back into deflation.
rows.why: 생산자물가는 급등하는데 소비자물가는 둔화되는 중국 사례를 통해, 에너지 같은 비용 충격(비용 인상 인플레이션)과 약한 국내 수요가 물가에 서로 다른 방향으로 작용한다는 원리를 배울 수 있다.
rows.why_en: China's case, with factory prices surging while consumer prices cool, shows how a cost shock such as energy and weak domestic demand can pull prices in opposite directions.
rows.term_def: A measure of changes in the prices producers charge for goods such as fuel and raw materials; it often hints at where consumer prices will go later.
rows.note: Cross-checked against Xinhua's report on the National Bureau of Statistics release of Nov. 9.

opinion.title: China's inflation cooled in October amid falling food prices
opinion.author: Lynn Song (Chief Economist, Greater China, ING)
opinion.summary: Song says falling food prices, down 2.9% year on year and led by vegetables, were the main reason consumer inflation slipped to 0.7%, while non-food inflation held at 1.5% on higher fuel and tech-component prices. Core CPI eased to 0.8%, a nine-month low, signalling that underlying demand remains soft even though China has left deflation behind this year. He calls the 5.7% PPI a new cycle high driven by coal, oil and gas, argues that persistently high producer prices should eventually reach consumers, and expects inflation to stay low but positive into 2027.
opinion.why: 원자재·에너지 가격 상승이 시차를 두고 소비자 가격으로 전가되는 과정과 근원물가의 의미를 전문가 분석으로 이해할 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: This expert analysis explains how rising raw-material and energy costs can reach consumer prices after a lag, and what core inflation says about underlying demand.
